newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat plantings sharply ahead of average.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat plantings sharply ahead of average.

text.p: Texas winter wheat plantings were running sharply ahead of average during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
Meanwhile, violent thunderstorms dropped heavy rains throughout central Texas, dampening cotton harvest prospects but providing good planting moisture for small grains.
Armyworms continued to be a problem in many pastures and were said to have begun moving into emerging small grain fields. Spraying operations continued as weather permitted.
Wheat planted 51 percent vs 32 year ago, 35 average.
Wheat emerged 23 percent vs 13 y/a, 15 avg.
Corn harvested 69 percent vs 75 y/a, 72 avg.
Corn mature 93 percent vs 90 y/a, 87 avg.
Sorghum harvested 61 percent vs 73 y/a, 71 avg.
Sorghum mature 77 percent vs 84 y/a, 79 avg.
Sorghum rated 69 pct good/excellent, 23 fair, 8 poor/v.poor.
Cotton bolls opening 47 percent vs 48 y/a, 46 avg.
Cotton harvested 17 percent vs 23 y/a, 23 avg.
Cotton rated 55 pct good/excellent, 26 fair, 19 poor/v.poor.
Pasture and range condition was rated 41 pct good to excellent, versus 36 percent at that level last week.
